tasks.description: Enforce rate limits using a token-bucket algorithm scoped to each API key. This will ensure each key gets an independent allowance. The algorithm should be designed to handle a high volume of requests.
acceptance_criteria: Given a valid API key, when a request is made within the allowed limit, then the request is processed successfully.

tasks.description: Make the bucket capacity and refill rate configurable via application configuration. This will allow for easy adjustments to the rate limits without requiring code changes.
acceptance_criteria: Given a valid configuration, when the rate limits are updated, then the new limits are applied correctly.

tasks.description: Store rate-limit counters/state in Redis to ensure limits are enforced consistently across all server instances. This will require setting up a Redis connection and implementing the necessary logic to store and retrieve the counters.
acceptance_criteria: Given a valid API key, when a request is made, then the counter is updated correctly in Redis.

tasks.description: Reject requests that exceed the rate limit with an HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests) status. This will inform the client that they have exceeded the allowed limit.
acceptance_criteria: Given a valid API key, when a request exceeds the rate limit, then a 429 response is returned.

tasks.description: Include a Retry-After header on 429 responses to indicate how long the client should wait before retrying. This will help the client to handle the rate limit correctly.
acceptance_criteria: Given a 429 response, when the Retry-After header is present, then the header contains the correct wait time.

tasks.description: Integrate the rate-limiting middleware with the existing API routes. This will ensure that the rate limits are applied uniformly to all authenticated API traffic.
acceptance_criteria: Given a valid API key, when a request is made, then the rate-limiting middleware is applied correctly.

tasks.description: Write unit tests to ensure the rate-limiting middleware is working correctly. This will include testing the token-bucket algorithm, configurable limits, and Redis-backed counters.
acceptance_criteria: Given a valid test suite, when the tests are run, then all tests pass.
